title: The quail and the hawk
hook: a quail safe in its own field is caught when it strays (SN 47.6)

segments.voice: Yesterday: six animals, the six senses, tied to one steady post. The post holds.

A hawk drops out of the sky and comes up with a quail in its claws. And the quail, being carried off, starts talking. Not begging. Scolding itself. This is my own fault, it says. I wandered out of my own range into somebody else's. If I'd stayed in my home ground, the ground my mother and father knew, this hawk would be no match for me. The hawk, apparently amused, asks: and where is this home ground of yours? A plowed field, says the quail, covered with clods of earth.
screen: `A QUAIL IN THE HAWK'S CLAWS.` → `I LEFT MY OWN GROUND.` → `A PLOWED FIELD, FULL OF CLODS.`

segments.voice: This is SN 47.6, in the Connected Discourses on mindfulness. The hawk, proud of its strength, lets the quail go. Fine, it says. Go home. Even there you won't escape me. The quail flies back to its plowed field, climbs onto a big clod of earth, and calls up: come and get me now, hawk. The hawk folds its wings and dives at full speed. The quail watches it come, and at the last moment slips down behind the clod. The hawk hits the earth breast first. Then the Buddha explains. Don't wander outside your own range, monks, into the range of others. In others' ground, Mara, the tempter, gets his chance. Others' range is the five cords of sense pleasure: sights, sounds, smells, tastes and touches that pull at desire. Your own range, the ground your fathers knew, is the four foundations of mindfulness: the body, feelings, the mind, and the patterns of experience. The quail isn't stronger than the hawk. It simply knows its ground, every furrow, every clod. Safety in this story isn't power; it's familiarity. And the text's word for range is gocara, a pasture, the ground a grazing animal knows by heart. Mindfulness isn't a fortress you build. It's a field you know so well you can disappear into it. The hawk doesn't stop being a hawk. What changes is where the quail is standing when one comes.
screen: `THE HAWK LETS THE QUAIL GO.` · `A CLOD IN A PLOWED FIELD.` · `YOUR RANGE: THE FOUR FOUNDATIONS.` · `GOCARA — A PASTURE KNOWN BY HEART.` · then, large: `YOUR OWN GROUND.`

segments.voice: Make your field small, the breath and the body sitting, and get to know its clods: where the breath touches first, where the body is heavy. When a thought flies off toward someone else's field, a plan, a worry, a screen, notice that you've left, and come back to one clod you know: one breath, one point of contact.
Gocara, range or pasture. Safety isn't strength; it's staying in your own range, the four foundations of mindfulness.
Your line: your own ground. The quail wins by knowing its field, not by being strong. Till tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 393 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE MONKEY AND THE PITCH.`

howItsDone: In many Buddhist communities, mindfulness is described as a practitioner's own ground or home base, returned to through the day; monastics often keep simple routines and guard the senses when they go into town as a way of staying in that range.

fork.setup: you're a quail, caught by a hawk. the hawk lets you go home, sure it can catch you anyway. what do you do?
options: fly as far away as you can
go to your plowed field, stand on a clod, and wait

fork.reveal: the quail stands on a clod in its own field and calls the hawk down. at the last moment it slips behind the clod, and the hawk hits the earth.

original.note: Pali gocara: range, pasture, the ground a grazing animal knows; the sutta's word for your own range.

trapdoor: what you thought: a fable about a lucky bird.
what it means: stay in your own range, the four foundations of mindfulness, and the hawk can't reach you.
what a scholar hears: gocara, a grazing ground, became a word for a monk's proper range; the quail calls its field its own ancestral domain, sake pettike visaye.

chat.says: How can mindfulness keep me safe if I'm not strong?
options: Like the quail: safety is knowing your own ground, not being strong.
By building a wall so strong that nothing can ever reach you.
By growing stronger than anything that could hunt you down.
chat.meaning: In SN 47.6 the quail escapes in its own plowed field. Your own range is the four foundations of mindfulness.

gocara.meaning: range, a pasture an animal knows by heart

five cords of sense pleasure.meaning: sights, sounds, smells, tastes and touches that pull at desire
